transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-07-07 15:00 UTC · Duration 48m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lina Park (CTO, Seabrook), James O'Neill (Head of ML), Priya Sharma (Platform)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Diego our SE and Ravi from customer success who may jump in later. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Lina: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to talk through model selection.
[00:15] James: Hi, yeah, looking forward. We sent over a one-pager with our use cases, hope you got it.
[00:20] Maya: Yep got it, thank you. Quick agenda: understand current stack, latency/cost constraints, multilingual needs, context length, tool-calling/function calling support, and then map to hosted/dedicated/private options and model candidates.
[00:30] Priya: That sounds good. For context, we run a customer support assistant + internal knowledge search and a live agent assist feature. Latency is important for live assist.
[00:37] Diego: Got it. Can you share current infra? Are you on cloud provider managed endpoints now or self-hosted?
[00:42] Lina: We use a mix. Frontend in GCP, some inference on GKE using HF transformers for small workloads. For heavy batch we run on EC2 with Triton.
[00:51] James: And we're evaluating moving to a platform where we don't have to manage GPU infra and also want to try larger open models for better accuracy.
[00:57] Maya: Perfect. On model selection, do you already have a preference for open models? We see customers considering Mistral, Llama-3 variants, Mixtral-ish, Manticore, and sometimes Bloom or Falcon.
[01:08] James: We ran small tests on Llama-2 and Llama-3 community weights. Results showed decent accuracy but cost was higher and latency sometimes spiky. We heard Mistral v2 performs well, and also curious about instruction-tuned Falcon variants.
[01:20] Diego: Important to note that performance varies a lot by sequence length and tokenization. Also quantization options (8-bit, 4-bit) will affect quality. For Hosted we have pre-quantized variants and perf profiles. For Dedicated you can bring custom quant artifacts too.
[01:33] Priya: Our main questions: Can Redwood hosted meet our P95 latency <500ms for short-turn live assist (<2k tokens)? And for long-context summarization (30k tokens) what's feasible?
[01:45] Diego: For hosted, typical short-turn on 8k context models can hit P95 ~200-350ms depending on model and batch. For 32k-like workloads, we recommend sequence-aware kernels and sometimes model variants with chunked attention; Dedicated or Private tends to give better predictability for those huge contexts.
[01:58] Maya: Also a routing policy can fall back to a cheaper model when latency spikes or burst capacity is limited. So you can keep SLAs without overpaying all the time.
[02:08] James: How about multilingual? We support customers in EU/ME/APAC. We need good support for Spanish, Portuguese, French, Japanese, and occasional Arabic. Which models do well out of the box?
[02:17] Diego: Mistral v2 and some Llama-3 instruction-tuned weights are quite multilingual. BLOOM has broad language coverage but is larger and costlier. We also provide fine-tuning and instruction-tuning options. If you have domain-specific docs, a small instruction-tune or retrieval-augmented pipeline helps a lot.
[02:33] Priya: Retrieval is key for us. We'll be doing RAG against a multi-tenant KB — can Redwood handle vector stores and embeddings?
[02:38] Maya: Yes — Redwood supports embeddings, and we have integrations with common vector stores; we also provide embedding models and suggestions for dimensionality/cost tradeoffs.
[02:46] Lina: Security question: SOC2, KMS, VPC peering for private deployment — what's the posture?
[02:52] Maya: We are SOC2 compliant; for Private we offer VPC with customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs. I'll share our security pack after the call (link).
[03:01] James: Can you also send over data retention and logs policies? Our legal team will review.
[03:06] Maya: Absolutely, sending the security & compliance docs (https://redwood.ai/security-pack.pdf).
[03:12] Diego: Back to models — function/tool calling. Do you need deterministic tool calls or open ended?
[03:17] James: Deterministic; we want structured JSON outputs for actions, and some multi-step tool workflows (query KB -> call internal search API -> format response).
[03:26] Diego: We support structured tool-calling and function schemas. Some community models have better alignment with function calling. For hosted we do function call orchestration in the runtime with retries and schema validation. For Dedicated you can run custom tool runners in the same VPC for lower latency.
[03:40] Priya: For on-prem or air-gapped compliance, is Private full-package available? How long to stand up?
[03:47] Maya: For full Private (on-prem), typical engagements are 6-10 weeks including delivery and security review. VPC-hosted private deployments can be faster — 2-4 weeks depending on networking.
[03:57] Lina: Interesting. Cost-wise what's the delta between Hosted and Dedicated for predictable 24/7 throughput?
[04:03] Maya: Hosted is pay-as-you-go; Dedicated gives reserved capacity discounts and more predictable per-token costs. We usually show a breakeven based on sustained throughput — Diego will share a modeler spreadsheet.
[04:15] Diego: I'll include example configs: dedicated pool size, autoscaling buffers, burst capacity, and expected P95 numbers. We'll show a sample that matches 200 reqs/sec of short-turn prompts vs 10 long summary jobs/hr.
[04:28] James: For benchmarks, what do you need from us to run realistic tests?
[04:32] Diego: Sample prompt sets, canonical responses or scoring rubric, expected concurrency pattern, and optionally a staging S3 with documents for retrieval so we can run RAG end-to-end.
[04:43] Priya: We'll prepare 2 prompt sets: live assist and long summary. Can you support 30k token context for the summary tests?
[04:49] Diego: We can run that; for 30k you may see higher latency — we'll test a 32k-tuned variant or chunked approach and show tradeoffs. Dedicated/Private will be more stable.
[04:59] James: Any model recommendations out of the gate for our use?
[05:03] Diego: Short list: Mistral v2 instruction-tuned (good mix of latency/quality), Llama-3 16k/32k variants for instruction-following, Falcon 180B-instruct variants if you need high few-shot generalization but it's heavier. For embeddings, use Redwood’s recommended smaller embed model for cost.
[05:18] Maya: We also provide Redwood-verified perf profiles so you can compare expected P95 and cost for each model variant.
[05:24] Lina: About model governance — do you allow pinning to specific model versions and audit of model changes?
[05:29] Maya: Yes, you can pin model versions, set rollout policies (canary/A-B) and we keep model change logs. For Private we can also freeze versions.
[05:36] James: One more question: can we bring our own model artifacts? We have a tuned Llama-3 model.
[05:41] Diego: Yes — Dedicated and Private allow BYO models; hosted can sometimes support private model uploads under enterprise arrangements. For BYO we need compatible quantization and weights format. We'll share the spec.
[05:51] Priya: Network: if we use Dedicated in our cloud, can you peer into our VPC? We prefer peering and private egress.
[05:58] Maya: Yes VPC peering is standard for Dedicated; private egress and customer-managed KMS are supported.
[06:04] Lina: For success criteria, we have three: quality (>= 90% on accuracy rubric), latency P95 < 500ms for live assist, and predictable monthly spend under target budget.
[06:15] James: We'll add some SLAs around model degradation alerts too — if quality drops we want rollbacks.
[06:21] Diego: We have quality monitoring tied to prompt sets/evals and regression alerts. We'll show how thresholds and alerting connect to rollouts.
[06:30] Maya: Recap: we'll send pricing, security docs, benchmark plan and schedule a technical deep dive. Any other concerns?
[06:37] Lina: Just one — training vs fine-tuning cost. For domain tuning how do you typically recommend?
[06:42] Diego: Often customers use retrieval augmentation first, then small instruction-tuning or LoRA-style fine-tune if needed. We'll estimate costs depending on model size and dataset.
[06:52] James: Ok great. Can we get an example throughput/cost comparison (hosted vs dedicated) for Mistral v2 and Llama-3 16k?
[06:59] Maya: Yes we'll include that in the spreadsheet.
[07:03] Priya: Timeline: goal to decide by end of July and start pilot in August.
[07:09] Maya: Sounds doable. We'll aim to have the benchmark plan and docs by 7/12 and the SE deep-dive week of 7/19.
[07:15] James: Thanks, appreciate it.
[07:18] Maya: Thank you all. We'll follow up with the links and next steps.
[07:22] 
Notes: occasional transcription artifacts: "Redwood dedicate" instead of Dedicated, "Mastro" for Mistral in one auto section; speaker labels sometimes generic in auto transcript.

[End of transcript]
